title: Friendship Theorem: Directed and Hypergraph Generalizations

problemStatement.formal: Directed friendship tournaments satisfy Longyear-Parsons regularity and n ≡ 3 (mod 4). STS(n) exists iff n ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 6). Spectral methods characterize regular friendship graphs.
problemStatement.plain: How does the Friendship Theorem extend to directed graphs and hypergraphs? We formalize directed friendship tournaments, Steiner triple systems, and spectral characterizations.
whyMatters: Extends the classical Erdos-Renyi-Sos result to directed and higher-order settings
Steiner triple systems are fundamental in combinatorial design theory
Connects friendship property to spectral graph theory and strongly regular graphs
Longyear-Parsons theorem reveals deep structure in directed friendship tournaments

axiomatized: longyear_parsons_tournament - directed friendship tournaments are regular (deep counting argument)
directed_friendship_mod4 - n ≡ 3 (mod 4) for directed friendship tournaments
directed_windmill_theorem - bidirectional directed friendship graphs are windmills
kirkman_existence - STS(n) exists iff n ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 6) (constructive, Bose/Skolem/Wilson)
spectral_friendship_characterization - regular friendship graph with k ≥ 2 forces k=2, n=3

insights: The 5 axioms are all deep results requiring infrastructure beyond current Mathlib
longyear_parsons_tournament requires double-counting argument with in/out-degree analysis
kirkman_existence is constructive (Bose 1939, Skolem 1958, Wilson 1975) - not provable by contradiction
spectral_friendship_characterization needs eigenvalue analysis of adjacency matrix
The Steiner counting lemmas (steiner_mod6_necessary etc.) are the strongest proved results
Set.ncard API is used throughout for cardinality of common neighbor sets
directed_friendship_mod4 depends on longyear_parsons - cannot be eliminated independently
